items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: hired me to come along with the trio along with Gene Krupa

ctx.x: That was dignity! But you as you say, with voice. were the first one musically, as far as I was concerned, and I've been watching you as long as you've been watching me, and I've seen your dignity -- and you're the first black musician that I've seen receive the dignity of a classical artist, the same respect that I would see for one of the great white musicians. And you did that, and you just brought it into a whole new different world. I don't now how it happened, but you did it.

Well, a lot of the exposure, I think, came from the Goodman, the spotlight thing was on the Goodman Trio because we were the first interracial organization in this country - we were 10 years before the sporting world, when the Goodman Trio came out of a recording studio, for years where there had been many mixed bands in the recording studio for years, but nobody played it live.
until the Goodman Trio was formed at the Congress Hotel in Chicago in 1936, when we played -- and the public spotlight was really on me, and Krupa and them.
